name: Coqui TTS Server
description: The tts-server HTTP demo shipped with Coqui TTS (coqui-ai/TTS, now community-maintained as idiap/coqui-ai-TTS). A Flask app serving a rendered HTML index plus REST synthesis endpoints on port 5002, binding all interfaces with no authentication. One of the cleanly Shodan http.html-visible TTS servers - the served index carries multiple Coqui-branded strings.
auth_notes: No authentication on any route. tts-server (TTS/server/server.py) is a Flask app started via app.run(host="::", port=5002) - it binds the IPv6 wildcard (and therefore also IPv4) on all interfaces by default. No API key, no token, no basic auth anywhere in the canonical server. Running with --debug enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which is remote code execution if exposed. Operators are expected to front with a reverse proxy for auth; the raw demo server has none.

shodan_dorks.query: port:5002 http.html:"Coqui AI TTS demo server"
shodan_dorks.rationale: The served index page contains the meta string 'Coqui AI TTS demo server' verbatim in server-rendered HTML - a direct, high-signal body match on the canonical port.
The Coqui logo asset filename coqui-log-green-TTS.png is hardcoded in the index template and appears in the served HTML body; nearly unique to this server across any port.
Conjunctive: the page title text 'TTS engine' plus the /api/tts synthesis path referenced in the index JavaScript pins the Coqui tts-server specifically and excludes other TTS demos.

The GitHub fork-ribbon link to coqui-ai/TTS in the index body confirms the canonical server; pair with a /details or model-name read for version scoping (Coqui shut down, so the idiap/coqui-ai-TTS fork carries current releases).

known_vulns: No authentication - unauthenticated GET/POST /api/tts?text= is an open synthesis and compute-exhaustion surface
style_wav parameter takes a file path or URL for GST reference audio, passed to the model loader - local file read / SSRF candidate worth verifying per build
Flask --debug mode exposes the Werkzeug interactive console = remote code execution if the operator enabled it
Binds the IPv6/IPv4 wildcard (host='::') by default - exposed to all interfaces out of the box
Werkzeug development server (not a production WSGI server) - no request hardening, trivially DoS-able
Full API self-documented via / and /details - free enumeration of voices, speakers, and languages
risk_notes: Coqui shut down as a company; the code lives on as the community fork idiap/coqui-ai-TTS (PyPI coqui-tts), so exposed servers span abandoned original installs and current fork installs. Vectors on an exposed instance: (1) Unauthenticated synthesis/compute theft via GET /api/tts?text= - any HTTP client drains operator GPU/CPU at zero cost, trivially scripted; (2) style_wav local-file-read / SSRF - the GST reference-audio parameter accepts a path or URL handed to the model loader, an unaudited file/network fetch surface; (3) Werkzeug debug-console RCE if --debug was left on; (4) voice/model enumeration via / and /details reveals loaded model identity for CVE scoping. Unlike the Gradio cohort this server is cleanly Shodan http.html-visible - the index page renders 'Coqui AI TTS demo server', the coqui-log-green-TTS.png asset, 'Type here...' / 'Synthesizing...' UI strings, and a github.com/coqui-ai/TTS ribbon in server-side HTML, so a body-string dork harvests it directly. Correction to a common assumption: the server header is Werkzeug/Flask, NOT TornadoServer.
deployment_notes: Launched via the tts-server console command or 'python3 TTS/server/server.py'; Flask app.run(host='::', port=5002) binds all interfaces. Server header is 'Werkzeug/<ver> Python/<ver>' (Flask dev server), not Tornado. First-party container images: ghcr.io/coqui-ai/tts and ghcr.io/coqui-ai/tts-cpu (docker run -p 5002:5002); the community fork ships ghcr.io/idiap/coqui-tts. The index JavaScript calls /api/tts?text={text}&speaker_id=&style_wav=&language_id= - multi-speaker and GST toggles (--use_multi_speaker) conditionally render speaker/language selectors. /api/tts_stream exists in some fork variants; treat /api/tts as the primary confirmed synthesis path. No TLS in the default configuration. The original coqui-ai/TTS repo is effectively frozen (~45.9k stars); active development and current PyPI releases come from idiap/coqui-ai-TTS.
